selector.rationale: The patient's presentation with acute urinary retention, hematemesis, progressive neurological deficits, and marked paraparesis, along with the presence of multiple bilateral symmetrical T2/FLAIR hyperintense lesions in the brain and diffuse T2 hyperintensities throughout the spinal cord, is most consistent with Acute Disseminated Encephalomyelitis (ADEM). The lack of albuminocytologic dissociation in the cerebrospinal fluid and the presence of normal sensory function also support this diagnosis. While Neuromyelitis Optica Spectrum Disorder (NMOSD) is a close runner-up, the patient's symptoms and imaging findings are more characteristic of ADEM.

rejected.label: Toxic Encephalopathy
rejected.why: Lack of clear evidence of toxic exposure and inconsistent imaging findings

rejected.label: Multiple Sclerosis (MS)
rejected.why: Atypical presentation and lack of characteristic MS lesions

rejected.label: Acute Transverse Myelitis
rejected.why: Limited spinal cord involvement and presence of brain lesions
